camera_mismatch_5z.code_reading: every strand input is camera-relative to the VP origin of its build's capture and rebased by +208 position differences (xfb_to_world.hlsl inverts the capture UBO's VP; hair_groom_update reads this build's soup; groom TLAS instances identity; header camera = the same UBO's +208, re-read at submit 0 differ; the G-buffer applies this frame's publish in 58-60 of 61 frames, org = 0). A one-frame build/render mismatch is excluded where the counters look (TLAS check 0, header/BLAS mismatch 0, build after the G-buffer 0, rt_hair_header_cam_gpu did not help in hc1). The moving-camera mode switches (bvhsplit.cpp 2626/2813/3459) only change holds, snapshots and row order (absent draws are not held: one key, not frame-wide). Left: the rays start at the VP origin (hp_rebase org, dir from inv(vp) of the near-plane point), right only while the eye sits at that origin; and frame 2066 (step about 0.4 m) did not trip.

fix_6a_stale_publish.cause: the game submits some G-buffer passes before their frame's scene build under fast camera motion; the newest publish ordered before them is the previous frame's (the builds rewrite points and BLASes in place, so it is the only consistent one). Its rebased trace (hp_rebase, org = camera step) lost the strands in exactly those frames; a still camera (org 0) never did.
fix_6a_stale_publish.fix: submit-time camera check (layer/hair_primary.cpp hair_primary_submit_begin): the applied publish's build camera against the G-buffer's own camera (its camera UBO +208, trusted when its VP eye is at the origin; else the build camera of its frame). Over 1 cm (hp_on_card's fixed band term) every recorded slot draws its card for that frame (existing card mode: card G-buffer and depth, no coverage evidence, no watchdog judgement).

The first 'stale publish:' lines name the offset (0.3-0.7 m) and the UBO camera against the build camera of the same frame (expected about 0: same camera block).

Then the rebase itself (why org = step loses the strands) is the next offline item. Trips remaining in frames not carded -> another stage; the stale lines tell which.

root_cause_6c.claim: The strand rays are rebased with a header camera read on the CPU (mapped camera UBO at the build's recording, rtscene.cpp rt_after_capture), while the groom points are converted on the GPU with that UBO as it is at execution, the same block the G-buffer's own draws read. Under motion the CPU read is sometimes the previous frame's camera: hp_rebase then starts every ray one camera step away from the eye although the points are already this frame's. Under a dolly the step lies along the view, so rays still hit but one step off the card: hp_on_card rejects them (rejected after the hit).
root_cause_6c.evidence_existing_logs: hc1 234025 (continuous turns): header camera copied on the GPU (rt_hair_header_cam_gpu=1) -> sampled origin exactly 0 in 18 of 18 fresh samples, strand share >= 0.93 in 15; CPU header camera -> origin 1-12 cm in 13 samples, share 0.13-0.94. hf1 073932 wheel zoom, G-buffer frame 2455: origin 0.496 m (0.445 m along the ray), strand share 0.029. Item 11's re-read at submit (0 differ) cannot see it: it reads the same mapped memory again.
root_cause_6c.withdrawn: 5z 'points and header camera describe one frame', 6a 'stale publish', item 11 'DISPROVED' (its hc1 trips were the shared-key dropouts, fixed since).

second_defect_6d.candidate: the header a G-buffer reads (groom TLAS, rows, key map) is one publish older than the points and BLASes the GPU holds: every build refits the BLASes in place, the older TLAS keeps the instance boxes of the previous camera-relative positions. With the right camera the rays then miss whole grooms whose box moved off the ray: sideways by step x tan(angle from the view axis), so small and off-centre heads lose everything, more with a larger step. This is what 6c's CPU camera lag looked like from the camera side.
second_defect_6d.instrument: build stamp (no shader): each build fills its header tag into a cell in its own command buffer; the G-buffer's command buffer copies the cell after its header copy; the count compares it with the publish applied. Trip lines end with 'groom points and BLASes on the GPU at that G-buffer: of ...', period line '[hair primary] build stamp (last N frames)'.

signatures.older header over newer BLASes (expected: trip lines say 'of a newer build' (stamp = applied + 1); period line in lower: newer >= the trip count; still windows may say newer too (harmless when still). Fix then: the submit-time pick must take that build's publish (find why ordered_publish does not see it), or the G-buffer must read the TLAS, rows and key map the last build wrote on the GPU, as rt_hair_header_cam_gpu does for the camera.
signatures.header and points agree: 'of the applied publish's build' on the trip lines: the TLAS is this build's. Then the per-groom loss is inside the build: LSS refit bounds after a large translation (test: rt_hair_groom full rebuilds in a moving window), or the LOD vote switching rows during the zoom (trip frames against 'LOD switches waiting' in the [hair groom] line).
signatures.build after the G-buffer: 'of an older build': the header is ahead of the points; the pick took a publish whose build had not run.

offline_6f.written: 2026-11-11, before the job was regenerated; no live since 003637
offline_6f.candidate_1_view_projection: By code the G-buffer side cannot disagree with itself: card point, ray direction, hit depth and card band all come from the draw's own camera block (gCam.vp). The points are the exact inverse of the prepass block's VP as its vertex shader applied it (xfb_to_world), so a jitter or projection difference between the two blocks moves no point. Left open only: the prepass block rewritten between its draws and the conversion, or a block whose VP is not view x projection.
offline_6f.candidate_2_entry_reuse: Ruled out for 003637's trips: G-buffer labels 2448-2452 each found the build stamp of their own label (5 of 5) and the builds are logged once per label 2447-2462, so no two G-buffers shared a label (and its seal) there. 000345 has a build label gap (2178 -> 2180) at its long frame: not ruled out for that one frame.
offline_6f.candidate_3_game_lod: In all 8 hl1 logs a new hair draw is first seen at the first trip frame or the one before and again 7 frames later (003637: 2447, 2454, 2456; trips 2448-2452). The arrivals are unmatched draws (not swapped); rows 12 -> 12, 0 rows with another key, 0 full BLAS builds in the trip frames; the loss lasts 5-7 frames and follows the step (000345: 2178/2179 trip after the long frame with no arrival). A coincidence of the zoom start, not the cause of the per-step loss.
offline_6f.decided: None of the three is shown to be the cause; no fix. The dense sampler decides.
